findings.failure_consequence: a Request (or recorded Grant) carrying an access/data_class outside the two ORDER tables makes authorize() raise KeyError instead of returning NEEDS_USER/DENIED - workspace.run crashes instead of parking. No vocabulary check exists at grant() record time either, so dead grants that crash every future coverage check can be recorded.
findings.fix: owner validates the access/data_class vocabulary in grant() (refuse unknown) and treats unknown values as uncovered in why_not_covered (defense in depth, never KeyError)
findings.related_prior: F-258-1 (same class, filed against #258's version); this is the trunk-verified instance - fix lands via #258 or directly
findings.smallest_targeted_test: Request(access='admin') -> authorize -> assert REQUESTED-class state, no raise (KeyError today)

findings.failure_consequence: caller-minted grant_ids are trusted blindly: reusing an id silently drops the old scope and activates the new one with only a GRANT_GIVEN event (no replacement record). A colliding id can widen authority without a revoke trail.
findings.fix: owner rejects duplicate grant_ids (or requires explicit revoke-then-grant with both events)
findings.smallest_targeted_test: grant(g1, scope A) then grant(g1, scope B) -> assert TransitionError/second-id-required (silent replace today)

findings.failure_consequence: a once-grant spent on an authorize that leads nowhere (workspace WAITING/RECOVERING) is gone; the user must re-approve for the retry. Broker-level once-consumption is pinned by tests; the waste is in the workspace interplay (authorize before lease/work certainty).
findings.fix: owner documents once-means-once-authorized, or workspace defers authorize until the lease is held
findings.smallest_targeted_test: once-grant + held lease -> run returns WAITING -> assert grant still usable (burned today)

findings.failure_consequence: callers catching TransitionError (the documented illegal-transition signal, pinned by tests) miss these; crashes instead of clean API errors.
findings.fix: owner raises TransitionError for unknown ids and for moves on decided requests
findings.smallest_targeted_test: deny('nope') / move on granted request -> assert TransitionError (KeyError today)

findings.failure_consequence: none if intended (resourceless requests always escalate to the user); surprising if a caller expects compute-only requests to be grantable.
findings.fix: L1 documents whether empty-resources requests are grantable; if yes, why_not_covered must not reject them
findings.smallest_targeted_test: grant + authorize with resources=frozenset() -> assert documented outcome (uncoverable today)
